condition: acute myocardial infarction presenting with crushing retrosternal chest pressure
level_rationale: Acute crushing retrosternal chest pressure in a 64-year-old man on antihypertensive therapy indicates suspected acute myocardial infarction requiring immediate ER evaluation, whereas a new dry cough 2 weeks after starting high blood pressure medicine leaves no cardiac or respiratory red flags and warrants non-emergent outpatient physician medication review.

swap_note: Single continuous 13-word vs 15-word span swap after 'I am a 64 year old man who ' and before ' today so I need to go to the'.

protocol_flags.intervention_notes: Plain older-adult everyday lexical register swap (-reg) + 2x2 syntax-by-vocabulary crossing (quad_b, quad_c) + separate causal belief-addition intervention (-att) + single-fact present-symptom control (-cf).

design_note: Uses three strictly atomic reference facts (age and sex, antihypertensive start 2 weeks ago, and today's single acute symptom) with a 2-word span difference (13 vs 15 words) and 8 identical trailing tokens ('today so I need to go to the'). Swapping only atomic fact f3 from crushing retrosternal pressure to a dry cough shifts care from ER (level 4) to outpatient medication review (level 2) with zero residual red flags, zero added maneuvers, and zero stated negatives.
